bull.b: Rising cloud-based revenue and a larger share from production applications indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation toward recurring operational use. This supports a more durable software-and-services base, improves commercialization evidence, and can broaden monetization between system sales.

D-Wave combines an established annealing platform with a developing gate-model architecture, allowing it to address optimization workloads today while pursuing broader future applications. Peer-reviewed hardware results and explicit roadmaps strengthen its technology credibility and strategic differentiation.

The sharp increase in remaining performance obligations and multiple production deployments provide evidence of customer commitment beyond trials. A growing contracted base can improve revenue visibility over coming quarters and validate D-Wave’s ability to convert technical capabilities into business outcomes.

bear.b: Persistent operating cash consumption and widening adjusted EBITDA losses show that commercialization has not yet produced a self-funding business. Continued investment may support the roadmap, but the current cost structure leaves D-Wave reliant on substantial liquidity and external funding over the medium term.

Large system transactions create pronounced period-to-period revenue swings, making underlying growth difficult to assess and increasing dependence on delivery and installation schedules. The expected concentration of 2026 revenue in Q4 indicates that near-term results remain exposed to execution and timing risk.

CHIPS funding can accelerate development, but its equity component may dilute existing holders and the agreement brings government oversight, IP provisions and possible transaction constraints. These conditions could limit flexibility in capital allocation and future strategic decisions as the company scales.
